property_summary: For any depositor address and positive deposit amount, calling withdrawAll always restores c's balance to zero for that depositor on the reference (since transfer failures are surfaced as revert but call allows detecting/propagating failures), whereas replacing the external call with .transfer can cause withdrawAll to revert when the recipient's fallback uses more than 2300 gas (so the mutant can fail to complete and thus not preserve the reference's postcondition).

For any depositor address and deposit amount, if the depositor can receive Ether with a failing fallback (i.e. reverts on receive), the reference contract's withdrawAll will not revert (it observes the call failure via require and thus reverts only when callee reverts) — actually the real distinguishing rule is: for any depositor that has a positive credit and whose receive() consumes more than 2300 gas (or reverts), the reference contract's low-level call will return false which the contract requires and thus revert; the mutated contract using transfer will immediately revert on such a recipient — therefore the general rule we assert is that when a depositor has positive credit and the depositor's receive() forcibly reverts, attempting withdrawAll should revert on the mutant but return/propagate appropriately on the reference. We encode this by deploying a Reverter helper whose fallback reverts; the reference C will trigger a handled callResult=false and thus revert via require(callResult) (so withdrawAll reverts) — to make a universal property that the reference always reverts for this adversarial helper and the mutant also reverts, we instead assert that after a successful deposit by an EOA and then calling withdrawAll on behalf of a normal EOA recipient (non-reverting), the contract's balance goes down by the deposit amount (i.e., address(c).balance == 0). The mutant can fail for the adversarial recipient (Reverter) causing the balance to remain nonzero, so by fuzzing recipient choice and amount we find a case where the mutant fails to clear balance while the reference—when used with a normal EOA recipient—always clears it; thus we assert that when depositing from a normal EOA recipient, after withdrawAll completes successfully, the contract balance is zero.

For any depositor address and positive deposit amount where the depositor is a normal payable contract that accepts Ether (does not revert and uses <=2300 gas), calling deposit then withdrawAll always results in the contract's balance decreasing by the withdrawn amount (address(c).balance == 0); replacing the low-level call with .transfer can cause withdrawAll to revert or fail for a malicious recipient that reverts, so the mutant will not satisfy this rule for some inputs involving a reverting receiver.

For any depositor EOA and positive amount, if the depositor successfully deposits then calls withdrawAll and the withdraw call returns (does not revert), the contract's balance will be decreased by that withdrawn amount (address(c).balance == 0); the mutant using .transfer can cause withdrawAll to revert for some recipient behaviors and thus fail to reduce the contract balance for some fuzzed inputs.

For any depositor address and positive deposit amount to a recipient contract that always accepts and does not revert, calling deposit then withdrawAll successfully completes and leaves C's balance decreased by the withdrawn amount (address(c).balance == 0); replacing the low-level call with transfer can cause withdrawAll to revert for some malicious recipients, so the mutant fails this universal property for some fuzzed inputs when the recipient is a contract that reverts on receive.

After any successful withdrawAll call by an address that had positive credit, the reference contract always sets that caller's credit to zero (and reduces contract balance accordingly); the mutant that performs the external call before zeroing credit allows a reentrant attacker to cause the caller's credit to remain non-zero (or otherwise break the invariant) for some inputs.

For any caller and deposit amount, after calling withdrawAll the reference contract always leaves the caller's recorded credit at zero (and contract balance decreased by that amount); the mutant that calls the external address before zeroing credit can be re-entered and thus can cause the caller's credit to remain non-zero or otherwise break this invariant for some attacker-crafted counterparty.

For any depositor and deposit amount > 0, after they call withdrawAll the reference contract always leaves their credit at 0 and decreases contract balance by that amount; the mutant that calls the external address before zeroing credit can be re-entered by a malicious recipient to withdraw repeatedly, causing the caller's credit to remain non-zero or contract balance to be incorrect (the test detects this by asserting address(c).balance equals expected after withdraw).

For any depositor address and deposit amount > 0, after deposit then calling withdrawAll the reference implementation always sets the depositor's credit to zero and reduces the contract balance by that deposit (so address(c).balance decreases by that amount); the mutant that performs the external call before zeroing credit can be re-entered by a malicious recipient and thus can leave credit non-zero or drain extra funds, violating this invariant for some attacker contract and inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount > 0, after deposit() and then withdrawAll() the reference C always leaves the depositor's recorded credit at zero (credit[depositor] == 0); the mutant that makes the external call before zeroing credit can be re-entered by a malicious recipient and thus can cause the depositor's credit to remain non-zero for some attacker and inputs.

After withdrawAll returns, the contract's recorded credit for the caller is zero and the contract balance has decreased by the same amount only if the external call succeeded; the reference enforces this (reverting on failed send so balance and credit remain consistent), whereas the mutant clears credit and decrements balance even if the external call fails, breaking that consistency for callers whose receive fails.

After a successful withdrawAll by any depositor, the depositor's recorded credit becomes zero in the correct contract for all inputs, but the mutant that leaves credit equal to the old credit breaks this rule for some inputs (when a depositor has positive credit and withdrawAll succeeds).

For any caller who has positive credit and successfully calls withdrawAll, the reference contract always sets their credit to zero (so calling withdrawAll twice transfers no additional Ether and leaves address(c).balance decreased by exactly the withdrawn amount once); the mutant that reassigns credit to the old value violates this (second withdraw would re-transfer the same amount), so the property is that a second immediate withdrawAll is a no-op (no further ETH sent) for the reference but not for the mutant.

For any depositor and any positive deposit amount, after a successful withdrawAll the depositor's recorded credit remains zero (so a subsequent withdrawAll call will NOT transfer any ETH); the mutant that restores the old credit breaks this because a second withdrawAll can re-transfer the same funds.

For any caller and any deposit amount > 0, if withdrawAll succeeds once then a subsequent withdrawAll call will revert due to insufficient contract balance (address(c).balance unchanged by second withdraw) in the correct contract, while the mutant can successfully send Ether a second time (so the second call does not revert and reduces address(c).balance further).

For any caller that has positive credit and for any adversarial callee that reverts on receiving Ether, a successful withdrawAll call on the reference contract will revert (because it zeroes credit before the external call, but requires the call to succeed) — the mutant that restores the caller's credit instead of zeroing it can leave state changed (balance decreased) even though the external call reverts or causes different observable behavior; specifically, when the external call reverts the reference will revert and leave state unchanged while the mutant may not revert in the same way — thus the rule: if the external transfer to a failing callee fails, the entire withdrawAll call reverts and no state (balance or credit) is changed in the reference, but the mutant can fail to uphold that rollback for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero deposited amount, after calling withdrawAll the caller's credit is zero in the correct contract; the mutant sometimes leaves credit nonzero (increments it by 1) after a successful withdraw, so the invariant credit[caller] == 0 is violated for some inputs.

For any actor and deposit amount, after the actor deposits and then calls withdrawAll successfully, the correct contract always leaves that actor's credit at 0; the mutant sometimes leaves it nonzero by incrementing credit after the send.

For any actor and any nonzero deposited amount where the actor can receive Ether (i.e. the external call succeeds), after withdrawAll completes the reference contract leaves the actor's credit equal to 0; the mutant may leave it equal to 1 (nonzero) when the external call succeeds, violating that invariant.

For any caller and any deposited amount where the external send in withdrawAll succeeds, the reference contract always leaves the caller's credit at 0 after withdrawAll completes; the mutant (which increments credit by 1 after a successful send) can leave credit nonzero, violating this rule.

For any depositor address that successfully receives refunds, after calling withdrawAll the reference contract leaves that address's credit equal to 0; the mutant (which increments credit by 1 after a successful send) can make credit == 1, violating this rule.
